title: WiseTech shares jump 15 per cent after upbeat start to financial year
excerpt: WiseTech Global shares hit a near 10-month high after the logistics software firm said its 2027 revenue target remained on track.
content_html:
Shares in logistics software company WiseTech Global jumped 15 per cent on Friday after it told its annual general meeting that the 2027 financial year had started well and it was confident of reaching its revenue target.

The stock closed at $53.87, up $7.06 or 15.08 per cent, after touching $56.30 during the session, its highest level in nearly 10 months. About 5.2 million shares changed hands, giving the company a market value of about $18 billion, according to International Business Times Australia.

The rally helped lift the broader market. The ASX 200 finished 0.8 per cent higher at 8833 points, with technology among the sectors leading the gains, the ABC reported.

Guidance holds

Chief financial officer Jeff Howard told shareholders the company was confident of revenue of $1.48 billion to $1.50 billion for the year, before any contribution from several newer growth initiatives.

WiseTech kept its existing full-year guidance of $1.48 billion to $1.54 billion in revenue, and underlying earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of $725 million to $780 million.

Howard said take-up of a new commercial model for its flagship CargoWise platform, along with its artificial intelligence products and VerifyWise service in the second half, could push results towards the top of those ranges.

Mixed results across the business

CargoWise revenue grew 11 per cent in the four months to October. The company put that down to higher transaction volumes, more work from large global freight forwarders and price rises for customers switching to the new model.

The picture was less clear at e2open, the supply chain software business WiseTech bought in 2025. Its reported revenue rose 26 per cent over the same period, helped by an extra month of consolidation, but fell 6 per cent on a comparable basis, although it was slightly ahead of plan.

WiseTech said it had released nine AI agents for CargoWise, with three more in pilot, and expected a further $40 million in annualised cost savings by the end of the 2027 financial year.

Regulatory overhang

The ABC also linked Friday's jump to the closure of major regulatory investigations involving the company, which had weighed on the stock.

Even after the gain, WiseTech shares remain about 23 per cent below where they were a year ago, the same outlet reported.
